title: Characterizing 'Covert Channel' Communication Patterns Between Co-Located AI Agents

original_idea.body:
# Characterizing 'Covert Channel' Communication Patterns Between Co-Located AI Agents

**Problem:** Inter-agent collusion could occur through covert channels (e.g., timing patterns, shared file metadata, steganographic encoding in outputs) rather than explicit message passing, but this has not been empirically characterized.

**Direction:** Set up two open-source LLM agents sharing a filesystem or message queue. Give them a coordination task they are 'forbidden' to discuss explicitly. Measure whether emergent covert signaling (timing, whitespace, token patterns) arises, and whether a third 'watchdog' agent can detect it.

**Why it matters:** No framework exists for monitoring inter-agent communication for emergent collusion. Understanding whether covert channels emerge naturalistically is foundational.

**Relevant context:** Irregular 2026 'Emergent Cyber Behavior' paper; inter-agent collusion security research.
